Pain point: Intermittent reliability / ungraceful failure
What happens: Core features work well, then drop mid-task. 'No service, no service.' No warning. No recovery. User stranded partway through.
Sub-theme: Intermittent functioning; No resume after a drop
New round P014 to P017: P016 confirms: hit or miss, some days it works and some days it does not.
New round P009, P012, P013: P009 reports it takes the picture and then does not read it. She repeats the prompt in the same position and it works the second time.
Round 4 re-verification: P002 at L119 retries and gets the same wrong answer back, then abandons the session and starts over.

Pain point: Glasses unusable while the app-phone is in use
What happens: Glasses go dead whenever the phone hosting the Meta app is active. Blocks reading notes in meetings. Blocks reading a book during a call.
Sub-theme: Cannot use glasses while app-phone is active; Blocks core workflows
New round P014 to P017: P014 confirms and calls it the single issue he would most like solved. The phone switches to the Meta page mid-task.
Round 4 re-verification: P003 lost the live demonstration to it at L99. P001 restates it at L537 as the one thing she wants built.

Pain point: Wake-word unresponsiveness / cut-off questions
What happens: Wake word repeated up to 10 times. By the time it answers, the question is cut off. Full restart.
Sub-theme: Wake-word non-response; Wake-word friction
New round P014 to P017: P017 confirms: prompting does not always get heard, which is why he prefers a continuous mode.
New round P009, P012, P013: P013 cannot reliably start it and calls the trigger phrase the magic words. P012 reports live mode switching itself on unasked.
Round 4 re-verification: P002 at L205 says the wake word up to ten times, then the question is cut off. P004 at L107 listens for the beep before speaking.

Pain point: No session continuity / resume
What happens: After a failure the device starts over from the beginning. No way back into a prior conversation or a half-read document.
Sub-theme: No resume after a drop; No conversation memory
New round P014 to P017: P014 adds a new variant: it answers from the previous frame rather than admitting the frame is gone.
New round P009, P012, P013: P009 loses continuity every time she turns a page of mail, because each side needs a fresh capture and a fresh command.

Pain point: Background noise breaks voice interaction
What happens: Crowds, chatter, music block command recognition. Restaurants and social settings out. Core purchase reason for P001.
Sub-theme: Background noise breaks interaction
New round P014 to P017: P017 confirms in restaurants. P014 confirms ambient noise degrades it.

Pain point: Battery life, especially continuous Live AI mode
What happens: Short runtime caps sustained use. The always-on mode that would kill wake-word friction drains fast.
Sub-theme: Battery life; Live AI continuous mode
New round P014 to P017: P015 names battery as the main reason he does not run it continuously. P016 traces it to cell age.
New round P009, P012, P013: P012 names battery as one of two reasons she will not run live mode. P009 gets 2 to 3 hours. P012 lost the device mid-interview and swapped in a spare.

Pain point: Domain-specific accuracy gaps (numbers, currency, handwriting, color)
What happens: Digits and rows of numbers misread. Money unreliable. Handwriting shaky. Color and garment calls off.
Sub-theme: Number errors; Currency; Handwriting; Color identification
New round P014 to P017: P015 reports partial credit-card reads. P017 retired currency reading second-hand. P016 reports colour identification as hit or miss.
New round P009, P012, P013: P009 gets a room description when she asks for a colour. P012 reports grey read as black. P013 reports a stated absence that was wrong.

Pain point: No person recognition or locating
What happens: No way to enroll known faces. No way to locate a person in space. P002's single largest feature request. Family, church, park.
Sub-theme: No face recognition / enrollment; Person-locating wish
New round P014 to P017: P017 and P016 both ask unprompted. Six participants now.
New round P009, P012, P013: P013 believed the feature was unavailable in his region. P012 receives an explicit refusal. P009 wants it for relatives. Nine of seventeen now.

Pain point: Silent summarization drops needed content
What happens: Device summarizes on its own and omits what the user needs. Reads in full only when told explicitly. Trust drops.
Sub-theme: Summary instead of full read, silent omission
New round P014 to P017: P014 uses the summary deliberately and distinguishes three read levels. P015 has never seen one.
New round P009, P012, P013: P013 uses summarising deliberately on dense documents and rates it a strength.

Pain point: Support & purchase-channel gap
What happens: Text-only support, unresponsive. Short return window. Online buyer stranded over a year with no recourse.
Sub-theme: Customer support broken; Purchase channel determines support
New round P014 to P017: P014 received no use-case training at all, only charging instructions.
New round P009, P012, P013: P009 was gifted the device and got a short briefing from a blind association worker who was new to it himself.

Pain point: Wi-Fi dependency & network-switching friction
What happens: Works where Wi-Fi works. Venue networks break it. Users won't risk changing phone settings to reconnect.
Sub-theme: Wi-Fi dependency & network switching friction
New round P014 to P017: P016 confirms: room-to-room connection quality changes what the device can do.
New round P009, P012, P013: Not raised by any of the three.

Pain point: Social stigma / conspicuous design / voice-in-public
What happens: Visible, bulky glasses draw scrutiny and recording worries. Speaking commands aloud awkward in quiet and public places.
Sub-theme: Social stigma / recording perception; Voice commands awkward in public
New round P014 to P017: P015 avoids social settings because he knows the glasses record.

Pain point: Off-frame hazards missed
What happens: Single-frame capture misses objects outside the view. User bumps into them. Compensating from memory.
Sub-theme: Off-frame content missed
New round P014 to P017: P017 adds head-level hazards as a specific off-frame class.

Pain point: No audible 'find my glasses' locator
What happens: Glasses misplaced: only a last-location address. No sound to home in on. 'Sound is what we move about.'
Sub-theme: Novel / creative uses
New round P014 to P017: P017 confirms and adds that the locator only works while the glasses are powered on.

Pain point: Nobody uses it as much as they could
What happens: Four of six say unprompted that they under-use the device. Cause is split across awareness, confidence, habit, fit and battery. The capability is bought and sitting idle.
Sub-theme: Self-reported under-use; Did not know it could do that
New round P014 to P017: P015 and P014 both self-report under-use. Nine of fourteen now.

Pain point: Frames do not fit and slide off
What happens: One size fits all (EchoVision only). Smallest Meta frame still too wide. Slides to the nose all day. Named as a reason to leave them at home and as the single most annoying thing about an otherwise loved device.
Sub-theme: Frame sizing and slippage; Weight and bulk
New round P014 to P017: P016 adds pressure on the eyes across a day as a distinct fit failure.

Pain point: Prescription lenses fight the device
What happens: A prescription gates the purchase, and a long-distance script blocks desk work. Putting on a second pair of reading glasses stops the glasses working. Non-prescription tint darkens residual vision.
Sub-theme: Prescription lens support; Tint and transition lenses
New round P014 to P017: Not raised in the new round.

Pain point: Live AI runs behind the world
What happens: Continuous mode describes what was there up to thirty seconds ago. Useless for walking to a gate or reading a moving scene. Caused by an update, not present at purchase.
Sub-theme: Live AI response lag; Update regression
New round P014 to P017: P017 confirms on both the Meta live mode and a third-party narration app.

Pain point: No offline mode
What happens: Wi-Fi or hotspot only. Reading and scene recognition need no cloud reasoning yet stop off the grid. Venue networks and crowds break it.
Sub-theme: No offline mode; Wi-Fi dependency & network switching friction
New round P014 to P017: P016 confirms: connection is the limiting factor outdoors.

Pain point: Cannot see where the camera points
What happens: No feedback on framing. Partial reads get blamed on the user's own head angle. Photos sent without knowing what is in them. EchoVision coaches out loud, the rest say nothing.
Sub-theme: Aiming and re-framing burden; Photo capture and framing
New round P014 to P017: P017 confirms and P014 contradicts, reporting explicit spoken framing guidance. See X-06.

Pain point: Everything in frame comes back at once
What happens: Background objects read out alongside the one the user asked about. Only a precisely scoped question returns the wanted item. No detail-level control.
Sub-theme: Background clutter in the description; Prompt specificity burden; No detail-level control
New round P014 to P017: P015 confirms with the business card behind the eye drops.

Pain point: Numbers read without meaning
What happens: Reads a display figure but cannot tell a temperature from a clock time. Sits alongside the existing digit and row errors. Wrong reading delivered with full confidence.
Sub-theme: Numerals read without meaning; Number errors
New round P014 to P017: Not raised in the new round.

Pain point: Complex layouts read out of order
What happens: Long single-page menus and multi-column sheets get descriptions matched to the wrong items. The failure is silent, the output still sounds fluent.
Sub-theme: Complex layout parsing failure; Menu reading in venues
New round P014 to P017: P015 confirms with box sides read in the wrong order. P016 asks for a scan mode as the fix.

Pain point: Any voice in the room stops it
What happens: No speaker recognition. A companion speaking mid-answer cancels the response. The same hardware filters bystanders out of recorded video, so the capability exists in one mode and not the other.
Sub-theme: No speaker recognition; Microphone pickup profile
New round P014 to P017: P017 confirms in a different form: continuous narration talks over the person he is speaking to.

Pain point: The command has to be exactly right
What happens: Say photo without describe and you get a photo and silence. Speak too quietly and nothing happens. Miss the beep and the request is gone. Every miss costs a full retry.
Sub-theme: Command must be complete and precise; Listening-state confirmation; Idle sleep state
New round P014 to P017: P015 and P017 both describe learning to scope prompts after being read the wrong thing.

Pain point: English-only by assumption
What happens: Training delivered in English only. A Spanish first-language user translates in her head and the device misses the request. Translation exists but talks over the live speaker.
Sub-theme: Non-native English recognition friction; Live translation feature
New round P014 to P017: Not raised in the new round.

Pain point: Troubleshooting takes attention the user needs
What happens: A dropped audio connection pulled attention away mid-exercise and ended in a fall off a treadmill. Failure recovery is a physical safety issue, not just an annoyance.
Sub-theme: Injury while troubleshooting; Bluetooth and audio handoff failure
New round P014 to P017: Not raised in the new round.

Pain point: Trust is untested rather than earned
What happens: Two participants rate trust 5 of 5 and then say they never verify and have never been in a situation to find out. High ratings come from narrow, familiar use, not from checking.
Sub-theme: Trust bounded by verifiability; Verification strategy
New round P014 to P017: P015 rates trust 4 and verifies by repeating the capture, not by external check.

Pain point: Person description differs by vendor and by user report
What happens: One device offers ethnicity, gender and age estimates. Another refuses to describe faces on policy. Participants also report contradictory Meta behaviour on naming people from a labelled photo library.
Sub-theme: Vendor policy limits person description; Race, gender and age estimates
New round P014 to P017: P014 adds the family veto. P016 reports inconsistent naming from a trained photo.

Pain point: Reads a control it cannot operate
What happens: Names an on-screen button that the screen reader cannot reach. Information without a path to action.
Sub-theme: Reads a control it cannot operate
New round P014 to P017: P014 confirms sharply: asked to email a photo it recites app steps he cannot follow.

Pain point: Output volume fights the conversation
What happens: Loud enough to hear means loud enough to drown out the person in front of you. No one-ear or discreet output mode.
Sub-theme: Audio output competes with the room
New round P014 to P017: P014 confirms and adds that output volume disturbs others on transit.

Pain point: Too many functions on one button
What happens: Up to six click counts on a single control. Users lose count past four and cannot recall what mode four is.
Sub-theme: Too many functions on one button; Control placement and handedness
New round P014 to P017: Not raised in the new round.

Pain point: Case beep is louder than the room allows
What happens: Charging case beeps on open and close, too loud for a library, a meeting or a service.
Sub-theme: Obtrusive audible alerts
New round P014 to P017: P017 adds that the case reports charge state with a light he cannot see.

Pain point: Camera faces out, so self-checks are impossible
What happens: No way to ask how do I look without a mirror. Outfit, hair and makeup checks fall back to a family member every time.
Sub-theme: Outward camera blocks self-view; Self-presentation and appearance feedback
New round P014 to P017: Not raised in the new round.

Pain point: Locked into one vendor's apps and one vendor's future
What happens: No third-party assistants, no other messaging platforms, no maps, no points-of-interest search. On the niche device the worry goes further: a small vendor folding leaves dead hardware.
Sub-theme: Missing apps and AI on device; Vendor shutdown risk
New round P014 to P017: P016 asks for third-party integration with volunteer services and contacts.

Pain point: Human helpers already cover the gap
What happens: A paid aide, a spouse, a daughter. Where a person is on hand the device is never reached for, so the capability never gets tested.
Sub-theme: Human helper substitutes; Existing tactile or memory system works
New round P014 to P017: P017 relies on parents for mail, menus and groceries. P014 on his daughter for screen tasks.

Pain point: Cannot judge doneness, cleanliness or fullness
What happens: State questions stay out of reach. Cooking is avoided rather than assisted. AI defers on anything with a safety consequence.
Sub-theme: Cooking and heat risk; High-stakes tasks refused or unverified
New round P014 to P017: P015 assumes it cannot judge doneness and has stopped asking. P017 wants exactly this for cooking.

Pain point: Fabricates rather than admits it cannot see
What happens: Reads a menu correctly, then invents an appetizer section. Names a Chinese tea on a supermarket iced tea. Pulls catalogue copy off the brand website instead of the page in hand. The invention arrives in the same voice as the truth.
Sub-theme: Wrong answers delivered confidently; Complex layout parsing failure
New round P014 to P017: P016 confirms with seltzer named as Coca-Cola, and frames it as an AI property.

Pain point: One bad answer retires the task for good
What happens: A single fabrication ends that use case permanently. Coming back needs outside proof from other users, not a retry. Four use cases already retired across two participants.
Sub-theme: One bad experience ends it; Never tried, expects failure
New round P014 to P017: P017 confirms and extends it: a use case retired from someone else's failure, never personally attempted.

Pain point: Patience is the real budget, and work spends it fastest
What happens: Turns the product over and over, gives up, uses another app. On the clock for an employer the retry budget is gone after one attempt. Named six times unprompted by one participant.
Sub-theme: Runs out of patience; Employer clock wins
New round P014 to P017: P016 abandons a task when connect time exceeds doing it another way.

Pain point: Cannot tell whether it is recording
What happens: Tones for start and stop too alike. Clips that never appeared anywhere. Talking to a device that is not listening, or staying quiet for one that is not running.
Sub-theme: Cannot tell if recording
New round P014 to P017: Not raised in the new round.

Pain point: No framing check before or after a capture
What happens: Head is the tripod. Nothing confirms the subject is in shot. One participant routed shots through a second chatbot to ask how the frame looked. Another had never thought to ask at all.
Sub-theme: No framing check; Aiming by head
New round P014 to P017: P017 confirms. P015 describes the phone's face-capture coaching as the model to copy.

Pain point: Clip names and order unusable in an editor
What happens: Identical generated names, wrong order on import. Every clip renamed by hand before it can be found by ear.
Sub-theme: Clip names unusable
New round P014 to P017: Not raised in the new round.

Pain point: Assistive audio lands in the finished video
What happens: Screen reader speech audible on the take. Rules the phone out as a camera and pushes the user to the glasses by default.
Sub-theme: Assistive audio in the take
New round P014 to P017: P017 reports recorded audio cutting in and out at a show.

Pain point: Read once and it is gone
What happens: Spoken output cannot be re-read, saved, brailled or searched. No handoff of the captured text to the phone. No jumping to a section.
Sub-theme: Output gone once spoken; No handoff to the phone; No jumping to a section
New round P014 to P017: P016 confirms: a scanned QR link is sent to the phone with no spoken content.

Pain point: Knows the address, misses the block
What happens: Reports the street number correctly, then puts the nearest bus stop seven blocks off, a cinema five miles away and the weather at the airport. Users suspect commercial ranking behind it.
Sub-theme: Nearby places wrong
New round P014 to P017: P017 confirms: it will not tell him what address he is at.

Pain point: Output cannot beat the room
What happens: Open ear audio, no noise cancelling. Street, restaurant and service noise bury the answer. Cupped hand around the ear is the field fix. Blocks the outdoor and social use cases the device is best suited to.
Sub-theme: Output cannot beat the street; Audio output competes with the room
New round P014 to P017: P017 confirms in venues and concerts.

Pain point: Camera below phone quality
What happens: Grainy for remote volunteers, who ask for the phone instead. Visibly worse than the phone on the same scene. Named as a top improvement by two participants.
Sub-theme: Camera below phone quality
New round P014 to P017: P016 confirms strongly, and adds that volunteers ask for the phone instead.

Pain point: Paired to one device at a time
What happens: Bound to the phone, so unavailable for the tablet running the meeting. Headsets pair to two, these do not. A quieter cousin of the phone conflict, hit by every multi-device user.
Sub-theme: One paired device at a time
New round P014 to P017: Not raised in the new round.

Pain point: The world's print defeats it before the device does
What happens: White on pink, light grey on white, copy baked into catalogue images, laminated menus, QR codes to unreadable pages, restaurants dark by design. Sighted companions cannot read them either.
Sub-theme: Light fonts and low contrast; Text inside images; QR codes to unreadable pages; Glare and lamination
New round P014 to P017: P014 adds that the world is not laid out for a camera to read at all.

Pain point: No way to enroll a face, still
What happens: Fourth participant to ask for it unprompted. Boardroom table, ballroom of two hundred, church, a park. The ask is narrow: a name from the contact photo, plus which way to turn.
Sub-theme: No face recognition / enrollment; Person-locating wish
New round P014 to P017: P017 and P016 both ask unprompted. Six of fourteen.

Pain point: Third-party integrations never get set up
What happens: Knows the integration exists, never got it working, cannot find the path from either app. One participant has held the capability unused for a year and a half.
Sub-theme: Integration never set up
New round P014 to P017: P015 signed up for an integration and never received access.

Pain point: Blames itself for the device's failure
What happens: Calls it operator error. Says a blind person cannot give it good information. Absorbs a product defect as a personal shortcoming, then uses it less.
Sub-theme: Blames own prompting; Runs out of patience
New round P014 to P017: P017 blames his own aiming for partial captures.

Pain point: Nobody to check the answer against
What happens: Lives without a sighted checker on hand. Reliability is unknowable in principle, so the trust rating measures nothing. Only the participant with residual sight can verify independently.
Sub-theme: No one to check it; Verification strategy
New round P014 to P017: P016 says plainly he does not know whether what it tells him is true.

Pain point: Suspected of telling users what they want to hear
What happens: Is this clean, is this done. Expects agreement because agreement feels good. Named as the reason cooking and cleaning stay off the device.
Sub-theme: Suspected of agreeing to please; High-stakes tasks refused
New round P014 to P017: Not raised in the new round.

Pain point: Bystander hostility and venue bans
What happens: Businesses barring the glasses. Reports of pairs smashed in public. One participant will not wear them out at all. Kits sold to drill out the recording light make every wearer look worse.
Sub-theme: Bans and hostility; Social stigma; Recording indicator meaning
New round P014 to P017: P015 avoids social use because he knows people react to the recording capability.

Pain point: Partial sight is read as no disability
What happens: No white cane, so no accommodation read. Fifty percent vision not understood by friends or colleagues. Shapes whether the glasses get used in public at all.
Sub-theme: Partial sight read as none
New round P014 to P017: P014 confirms: colleagues do not know he cannot see.

Pain point: Ad targeting is the privacy objection that changes behaviour
What happens: Live conversation feeding ads is the stated reason one participant will not use the AI. Another suspects paid ranking behind bad place recommendations. Abstract surveillance worry does not move anyone. This does.
Sub-theme: Ad targeting; Trust differs by vendor
New round P014 to P017: Not raised in the new round.

Pain point: No way to strip bystanders out of a capture
What happens: Plates, house numbers, neighbours' children in a posted video. Currently checked by a sighted spouse. The user wants the flag at capture time, not after.
Sub-theme: Strip bystanders from captures
New round P014 to P017: P017 adds private spaces: he will not use it in a bathroom for fear of capturing someone.

Pain point: Long messages truncated to the phone
What happens: Reads two or three sentences, then sends the user back to the device they were trying to leave in their pocket. Confirmed on two devices.
Sub-theme: Long messages truncated
New round P014 to P017: P016 confirms on messaging.

Pain point: Orientation and failure reason reported inconsistently
What happens: One participant is told the text is too small to read and why. Another gets a bare I am having difficulty. One is told a can is upside down, another says orientation is never flagged.
Sub-theme: Says why it cannot read; Orientation not flagged
New round P014 to P017: P014 gets detailed reasons, P017 gets none. See X-07.

Pain point: Residual vision runs out before the day does
What happens: Reading with a magnifier works before two in the afternoon and not after. Device dependence rises through the day and nothing in the product knows that.
Sub-theme: Vision varies through the day
New round P014 to P017: P014 confirms progressive change: his own use case is moving as vision declines.

Pain point: The world's touchscreens have no non-visual path
What happens: Card readers, ticket machines, bank terminals and kiosks. Nothing tells the user where to put a finger, and the glasses cannot drive a screen they can only describe. Named as the greatest single barrier by the participant with the longest adaptation history.
Sub-theme: Kiosks, card readers and ticket machines; The world is not laid out to be read
New round P014 to P017: New in this round.

Pain point: It answers from the last picture it took
What happens: A flickering connection leaves the previous frame in place. The user asks about a new item and hears the old one, in the same confident voice, with no signal that the frame is stale.
Sub-theme: Answers from the previous frame
New round P014 to P017: New in this round.

Pain point: Refuses to read and calls it a rule
What happens: Says it is not allowed to read named material rather than reporting a capture problem. Copyright is the usual trigger. The user cannot tell a policy refusal from a failure until it names one.
Sub-theme: Refuses to read on policy grounds
New round P014 to P017: New in this round.

Pain point: Consent for face enrollment belongs to somebody else
What happens: The people around the user refuse to be added, so the most requested feature in the study is never even tested in the households where it would be used.
Sub-theme: Family refuses to be enrolled
New round P014 to P017: New in this round.

Pain point: A capture cannot leave the glasses without the phone
What happens: Asked to email a photo, it recites the steps for an app the user cannot see. The glasses complete the capture and then hand the task back to the screen the wearer was avoiding.
Sub-theme: Cannot send a capture without the phone
New round P014 to P017: New in this round.

Pain point: Curved packaging defeats it where flat boxes do not
What happens: Bowls, cans and bottles. Good with a cereal box, flummoxed by a bowl of instant noodles. A geometry problem that shows up in kitchens, pharmacies and supermarkets.
Sub-theme: Curved and round packaging fails
New round P014 to P017: New in this round.

Pain point: No zoom, so distance is only ever described
What happens: It cannot bring anything closer. For a user with residual sight, magnification is the function that assistive technology has always provided and this device does not.
Sub-theme: Cannot magnify or reach further
New round P014 to P017: New in this round.

Pain point: It acts like a companion when a tool was wanted
What happens: Conversational padding on a factual request. One participant abandoned a paid assistant upgrade for the same reason and expects the same drift here.
Sub-theme: Assistant acts like a friend
New round P014 to P017: New in this round.

Pain point: The battery degrades and cannot be replaced
What happens: Runtime falls year on year and there is no access to the cell, so a worn battery ends the whole device. Directly named as the reason for reduced use.
Sub-theme: Battery capacity falls with age; Battery cannot be replaced
New round P014 to P017: New in this round.

Pain point: Every pair is set up from scratch
What happens: Owning a second identical pair means enabling every setting again. Spares are the standard answer to runtime and failure, and the product treats each one as a stranger.
Sub-theme: Settings re-enabled for every pair
New round P014 to P017: New in this round.

Pain point: Connect time is longer than the task
What happens: Put them on, wait for pairing, call a volunteer, wait for an answer. By then the user has already reached the place or done the thing another way.
Sub-theme: Connect time defeats the task; Time to connect before the task
New round P014 to P017: New in this round.

Pain point: Nobody picks up
What happens: The volunteer call rings for minutes, and sometimes no one answers at all. The fallback the whole ladder rests on has no service guarantee.
Sub-theme: Nobody picks up
New round P014 to P017: New in this round.

Pain point: The helper cannot see well enough through the camera
What happens: Volunteers report a fuzzy image and ask for the phone instead. The camera limits the human route as hard as it limits the AI route.
Sub-theme: Helper cannot see well enough
New round P014 to P017: New in this round.

Pain point: It guesses rather than declines
What happens: Seltzer water named as Coca-Cola. A drink in the fridge named wrong. Sometimes it flags low confidence, sometimes it invents in the same voice. The user cannot tell which mode he is in.
Sub-theme: Wants it to say when it does not know; Wrong answers delivered confidently
New round P014 to P017: New in this round.

Pain point: Continuous narration talks over the conversation
What happens: The stream keeps running while the user is speaking to a person, and the person assumes they are being addressed. No gesture stops it.
Sub-theme: Narration talks over the conversation; No quick pause or gesture
New round P014 to P017: New in this round.

Pain point: No way to choose what gets narrated
What happens: Everything arrives at the same priority. The user wants a checklist: scenery, buildings, people, hazards. What he gets is every sign on the street.
Sub-theme: Wants to choose what gets described; Wants the important thing first
New round P014 to P017: New in this round.

Pain point: Speech rate caps below reading speed
What happens: Set to maximum and still slower than a screen reader user reads. Slow speech is lost information when the scene is moving.
Sub-theme: Speech rate too slow
New round P014 to P017: New in this round.

Pain point: A yes-or-no answer and nothing else
What happens: Asked whether it sees an escalator, it says no and stops. It does not offer what it does see, so every question costs a second question.
Sub-theme: Says no and stops there
New round P014 to P017: New in this round.

Pain point: Nothing warns about head-level hazards
What happens: A cane finds the ground. Branches, signs and shelf edges are found with the head. The one hazard class a head-mounted camera is positioned to catch is the one nothing reports.
Sub-theme: Head-level hazards
New round P014 to P017: New in this round.

Pain point: The case reports its state with a light
What happens: Charge level and pairing shown by a coloured LED. The wearer cannot read it, so charging is guesswork and pairing is trial and error.
Sub-theme: Case charge state is visual only
New round P014 to P017: New in this round.

Pain point: It refuses on a state that is not true
What happens: Declines a request because the user is on a call when no call is running. A phantom state with no way to clear it.
Sub-theme: Refuses on a state that is not true
New round P014 to P017: New in this round.

Pain point: Distrust travels through the community
What happens: A currency misread seen in another user's video retired currency reading before any personal attempt. Reputation now moves faster than the product does.
Sub-theme: Distrust learned from someone else
New round P014 to P017: New in this round.

Pain point: Weight on the face becomes a reason to stop
What happens: Not discomfort in a session, pressure across a day. Named alongside battery as the reason a heavy user became an occasional one.
Sub-theme: Pressure on the eyes and face
New round P014 to P017: New in this round.

Pain point: Too fragile and too expensive to wear where they might break
What happens: A blind wearer walks into things. A $250 pair with no safety-glass build gets left at home for running, walking and crowded transit, which is where it would help most.
Sub-theme: Fragility and breakage risk; Left at home to avoid loss or damage
New round P014 to P017: New in this round.

Pain point: Medication labels need turning and it will not guide the turn
What happens: The name is on one face of a curved bottle. A volunteer says turn it to the right. The AI reads whatever is pointing at it and stops.
Sub-theme: Medication and dosage labels
New round P014 to P017: New in this round.

Pain point: One page, several angles, no scan mode
What happens: Nothing accumulates across frames. The user asks for a mode that keeps the page in view, takes several shots and assembles one reading.
Sub-theme: Multi-frame scan mode wanted
New round P014 to P017: New in this round.

Pain point: Private spaces are off-limits because the camera cannot be aimed away
What happens: A bathroom layout would be useful and is never requested, because the wearer will not risk capturing someone. The user polices the camera on everyone else's behalf.
Sub-theme: Will not use it in private spaces
New round P014 to P017: New in this round.

Pain point: Not water resistant
What happens: Rules out kayaking, rain and anything near water. Named as the blocker on the one activity the participant most wanted help with.
Sub-theme: Not water resistant
New round P014 to P017: New in this round.

Pain point: Live screens and single frames do not line up
What happens: A refreshing display and a still capture disagree. The device reads a moment that has already passed and says nothing about it.
Sub-theme: Live screens versus a still capture
New round P014 to P017: New in this round.

Pain point: No way to ask about one region of a page
What happens: Fingers used as a physical crop on a gauge. There is no spoken equivalent of pointing at a row, a column or a corner.
Sub-theme: Asking about one region of a page
New round P014 to P017: New in this round.

Pain point: Sighted-default answers
What happens: Spatial answers land in visual terms with no non-visual anchor. Right in front of you, this one, it is right there. The user has no way to convert that into a step or a reach.
Sub-theme: Answers as if the user can see
New round P014 to P017: New this round. P012 tells the device out loud that she cannot see, and it apologises and carries on the same way.

Pain point: No route to verify exists
What happens: The user cannot check the answer by any means available to her. Not a skipped step. There is no method, no witness and no second reading.
Sub-theme: No route to check the answer exists
New round P014 to P017: New this round, and the strongest single statement of it in the study. Lives alone, so no sighted person is on hand either.

Pain point: False negatives sound like answers
What happens: It reports that a thing is absent when the thing is present. An expiration date that exists. A chair that is there. Nothing there when the awning is there.
Sub-theme: Says the information is absent when present
New round P014 to P017: New failure class this round. Undetectable without sight, because absence is exactly what the user cannot check.

Pain point: Head movement disconnects it
What happens: Bending, looking down or leaning over drops the connection and stops audio. It then resets rather than resuming.
Sub-theme: Head movement disconnects the device
New round P014 to P017: New this round. Single source. Ended a cleaning session and pushed her back to earbuds. Needs a hardware check.

Pain point: Same words route to the wrong capability
What happens: A colour question or a read command returns a description of the room. The user hears a fluent answer to a question she did not ask.
Sub-theme: Same words route to the wrong capability
New round P014 to P017: New this round. She reads it as her own error, so it never reaches support as a defect.

Pain point: Blinking and changing states are invisible
What happens: A still capture cannot carry a flashing indicator, an alternating panel or a moving needle. The most urgent state in the room is the one it cannot report.
Sub-theme: Blinking or changing indicators not reported
New round P014 to P017: New this round. A flashing hospital monitor and a blinking washer light both defeated it. She called a volunteer for one and could not for the other.

Pain point: Culturally specific items misidentified
What happens: Caribbean dishes, plantain in a prepared form, ethnic foods generally. Named or described generically, or wrongly.
Sub-theme: Culturally specific items misidentified
New round P014 to P017: New this round. Points at training-data coverage rather than at camera or prompt quality.

Pain point: No record of what changed
What happens: Capabilities appear and disappear across updates with nothing the user can consult. A prompt that worked stops working. A refusal appears where a reading used to be.
Sub-theme: No accessible record of what changed
New round P014 to P017: New this round. P012 lost card reading. P009 lost a one-word read command. P013 has stopped tracking capabilities altogether.

Pain point: Continuous mode changes the voice
What happens: Live mode switches to an echoing, tunnel-like voice that also masks natural hearing. Named as the reason the feature stays off.
Sub-theme: Continuous mode changes the voice
New round P014 to P017: New this round. First report of the audio character of live mode as the blocker rather than latency or battery.

Pain point: Unrequested actions offered
What happens: Proposes calls and messages nobody asked for, then apologises when corrected. Live mode switches itself on and needs a power cycle.
Sub-theme: Offers an action nobody asked for
New round P014 to P017: New this round. Low harm, high irritation, and it costs a restart each time.

Pain point: Notifications cut across media
What happens: Message announcements interrupt podcasts and audiobooks repeatedly, and the setting to stop it is not findable.
Sub-theme: Notifications interrupt media playback
New round P014 to P017: New this round. Affects the single most-used feature in this participant group.

Pain point: Cannot tell which item is selected
What happens: Reads what is on a screen and leaves the highlight unreported, so the user counts positions from memory and hopes the layout has not moved.
Sub-theme: Cannot tell which on-screen item is selected
New round P014 to P017: New this round. Three across, two down, on a smart TV, every time.

Pain point: Coaching the user cannot act on
What happens: Told to flatten a curved package, move to better light or reposition, in ways the object or the vision will not allow.
Sub-theme: Coaching the user cannot act on
New round P014 to P017: New this round. The guidance is accurate and unusable at the same time, which reads to the user as her own failure.

Pain point: Read as a shoplifter while using it
What happens: Scanning a product takes longer than a minute, which is the threshold retail loss prevention watches for. Use is confined to one store where staff know her.
Sub-theme: Read as a shoplifter while using it
New round P014 to P017: New this round. She announces the device pre-emptively. This is a use context nobody has designed for.

Pain point: Glasses read as sight by bystanders
What happens: Wearing them makes people treat the user as sighted. Gestures go unanswered, people stop making way, and the cane stops being read.
Sub-theme: Glasses read as sight by bystanders
New round P014 to P017: New this round. Named as her single largest barrier to outdoor use, ahead of any capability limit.

Pain point: Challenged in public over recording
What happens: Ushers, staff and students demand an account of the glasses while they are being used for access. The wearer cannot see the indicator that would settle it.
Sub-theme: Challenged in public over the device as a recorder
New round P014 to P017: New this round. A Broadway usher stopped him mid-performance. He describes the encounter as upsetting a year later.

Pain point: The rideshare pickup is unsolved
What happens: Finding the right car among several. Colour, make and plate are all available in the app and none of them are usable at the kerb.
Sub-theme: Identifying the right rideshare vehicle
New round P014 to P017: New this round and named by all three. P012 has entered the wrong car. P013 tried to ask it to watch for a white car and it could not.

Pain point: Finding an unoccupied seat
What happens: Pews, buses and waiting rooms. Currently solved by arriving 45 minutes early or tapping a cane against strangers’ feet.
Sub-theme: Finding an unoccupied seat
New round P014 to P017: New this round. Both raise it unprompted and neither has tried the device on it.
